title: When Does Continual Pre-Training Help? An Empirical Study of Decoupled Knowledge and Generation Trajectories in Clinical LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2611.30507v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Continual pre-training (\textit{CPT}) is a standard route for domain adaptation, yet existing studies typically track pre-training loss or multiple-choice question answering (\textit{MCQA}) accuracy alone, offering only a narrow view of how adaptation unfolds. We jointly track factual knowledge via \textit{MCQA} and open-ended behavior via pairwise preference rankings across $18$ checkpoints for each of eight instruction-tuned \textit{Qwen} models ($0.5B$ to $8B$), adapted to German medicine with \textit{CPT} and \textit{SLERP} merging. The two axes converge at consistently different rates, with preference rankings reaching $90\%$ of their total gain after a median of $1.7B$ tokens versus $3.5B$ for \textit{MCQA}. A judge-free token-distribution measure reaches this threshold at $1.9B$ tokens. Per-aspect scores indicate that these early preference gains largely reflect surface alignment, meaning models can sound domain-appropriate before

translated_title: 持续预训练何时有帮助？临床大语言模型中解耦的知识与生成轨迹的实证研究
translated_abstract: 持续预训练（CPT）是领域适应的标准途径，然而现有研究通常仅跟踪预训练损失或多选题问答（MCQA）准确率，对适应过程如何展开只能提供狭隘的视角。我们通过MCQA联合跟踪事实知识，并通过成对偏好排序跟踪开放式行为，覆盖八个指令微调的Qwen模型（0.5B至8B）各自的18个检查点，这些模型通过持续预训练和SLERP合并适应德国医学领域。这两个维度以持续不同的速率收敛：偏好排序在约1.7B tokens（中位数）后达到其总增益的90%，而MCQA则需要3.5B tokens。一个无需评判者的token分布度量在1.9B tokens时达到该阈值。逐方面的得分表明，这些早期的偏好增益主要反映了表面层面的对齐，这意味着模型在真正掌握领域知识之前就可能已经表现出符合领域风格的表达。
tldr: 该研究通过同时跟踪多选题知识测试与开放式生成偏好排序两条轨迹，发现临床大语言模型持续预训练中生成风格对齐的收敛速度（约1.7B tokens）显著快于事实知识的获取（约3.5B tokens），且早期生成增益主要源于表面层面的领域风格对齐。
en_tdlr: By jointly tracking MCQA factual knowledge and open-ended preference rankings across 144 checkpoints of Qwen models adapted to German medicine, this study reveals that generation-style alignment converges about twice as fast as factual knowledge acquisition during continual pre-training, with early generation gains largely reflecting surface domain-style alignment.
